denominator: every game he appears in (union denominator)

rate_gates.why: A college rate is computed over the games he appears in, which can miss a game he played quietly. That error was measured in the NFL, where the true figure is known: median 0.2 points, 90th percentile 3.8. It is largest at short reception lines, so those carry no rate, and a market that was never measured carries none either.

single_day_rule: This board is 2026-09-10 only. Priced rows for another day are not shown here and neither are parlays that would cross days — a card dated one day and half-filled with the next is two facts under one label. Minimum 5, maximum 50; a day with no games is an empty board, and that is correct.
empty_reason: No College Football picks for 2026-09-10. Nothing is priced for this day yet. An empty board on a day with no games is the correct result, not a failure — the card was built and it found nothing to show.

board_rule: Sorted by the player's own record at that exact line, highest first — the same order the MLB board uses. Rows with no record sit below every row that has one.
no_model_note: 🔴 No row on this board carries a Gizmo's confidence rating and none ever will on today's evidence. Three pre-registered football models were tested and every one lost to a player's own season average. What is shown is his OWN RECORD and the market's price — both labelled.
college_note: College records are counted over the games a player appears in. College box scores list him only when he did something, so a game he played quietly can be missing — which nudges an over slightly high. That gap was measured against the NFL, where the true figure is known: a median of 0.2 percentage points and 3.8 at the 90th percentile. Short reception lines, where the gap is biggest, carry no record at all.
schema_note: Renders through the same pickCard component as the MLB board. confidence_basis is RECORD or MARKET, never MODEL.
